Two FruitBars cost £1.50 without buying a BarBox.

Here are the necessary calculations, which require some algebra:
Barbox, which can be written as B, Fruitbar = F, Oatbar = O = £1.75, ‘A barbox is twice as expensive as 3 Fruitbars,’ hence, the following formula can be created:
B = 2 x (3F), which can be simplified to; B = 6F
A second formula can be created as a ‘Barbox combines two of each type of bar and is £0.50 cheaper than buying them individually:’ B = 2F + 2O - £0.50 As B is equivalent to either equation, the two equations can be combined together to eliminate the algebraic variable; B. These are called simultaneous equations and are encountered at GCSE Maths.
6F = 2F + 2O - £0.50
Via a simple rearrangement and simplification of the equation we arrive at:
6F – 2F = 2O - £0.50
4F = 2O - £0.50
We know that an Oatbar is £1.75, hence two Oatbars (2O = 2 x £1.75) cost £3.50.
Therefore, following more rearrangements and simplifications;
4F = £3.50 - £0.50
4F = £3.00
F = £3.00/4
F = £0.75.
A BarBox will cost less than 5 FruitBars.

a. We do not need to know the price of either FruitBar or BarBox to know that this is false. Given that BarBoxes are twice as expensive as 3 FruitBars, or in other words, 6 FruitBars, they will cost more than 5 FruitBars. As such, this statement is false.
BarBoxes have sold less than OatBars.

a. We are not given exact sales figures. However, we are given the relationships between the bars sold. b.
Barbox combines two of each (2 x Oatbars + 2 x Fruitbars)
Half of Oatbar sales are sold through Barboxes. c.
If 2 are sold each time as part of the Barbox, and this represents half of the sales of Oatbars, then 4 oatbars are sold each time a Barbox purchase is made. d.
Hence, 4 times as many Oatbars are sold as Barboxes themselves (including the ones sold through the Barbox), or twice as many oatbars are sold, excluding the ones sold through Barboxes. e.
In either case more Oatbars are sold than Barboxes. Barboxes have sold less than
OatBars. f.
Thus, the answer to the question is "True," also considering that "sold" implies that sales have been made, so, the sales figure must be greater than 0 and follow the relationships described above.

a. Charles’ children will use at least 4 devices. Therefore, the plan cannot have less than 4 devices. It also can only be 12 months. Only Hare and Dog fit this profile. And the one that is cheapest is Dog. Therefore, Dog is the correct answer.

a. Since 1m2 of Wood costs £90, then 5m2 will cost 5 times this = £450. b.

This question asked you which statement was incorrect. a. Only two possible contracts have an annual salary where one is half of the other.
These are Alpha, (10,000) and Beta (20,000). Since Beta is the contract which earns twice as much as Alpha, this is the one Lucy has.
Debra has a Foxtrot contract and Lucas a Beta contract. How much more money at the end of the contract does Debra earn than Lucas?

a. The key to working out this calculation is the contract length. Foxtrot is for 24 months, which means that Debra will get paid the Foxtrot annual salary twice. We subtract 10,000 from 200,000 to get the difference= 190,000.
